title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: There are now three (3) main trade union federations in Namibia. The proliferation of trade unions also cascaded to the sectors with the resultant competition for memberships and operating spaces undermining the influence of trade unions. Membership levels have also declined due to increasing “casualization” of work, the increase in ‘flexible’ forms of employment and informalization of the economy. Some of the federations and unions have not renewed their leadership in years due to organisational inadequacies which has weakened their influence on policies and participation in key policy and legislative processes. Despite these challenges, trade unions have over the years been involved in tripartite programmes under the banner of the framework of the DWCP on HIV/AIDS, OSH, social security, commission on minimum wages for domestic workers and development of the Namibian National Employment Policy (NEP). The ILO has taken efforts to introduce trade unions and their leadership in dialogues and engagements on UN programmes through the UNSDCF development including discussions and processes on the CCA, NDCs, The Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions and SDG implementation through the Resident Coordinator’s Office. In the 2024-2025 biennium, ILO support will focus increasing institutional, technical, representational and policy impact capacities of workers' organizations to participate and contribute to national and sectoral policy and legislative development. This will include support to develop proposals to be considered in social dialogue mechanism for policy making.
